# shibbo

> A dialect atlas of machine writing. shibbo keeps a dated, sourced registry of AI tells (patterns that mark text, code, interfaces and agent behavior as machine-made), measures how often each GPT, Claude and Gemini release uses the prose tells compared with human writers on the same topics, and checks your own work against the current list.

- Every entry cites at least one source: measured studies (Graphite's AI Tells, Kobak et al.), community lists (Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing) and open-source checkers. shibbo gathers them into one registry.
- Tells change with each release. In 2024 "delve" gave away GPT-4; by 2026 most models use it no more than people do, and newer ones have their own habits.
- shibbo is an editor, not a detector: a clean score means a draft avoids known tells and says nothing about who wrote it.
- Install: `npx shibbo check <file>`; `npx shibbo init <harness>` sets up Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and other harnesses; `npx shibbo mcp` starts an MCP server.

## Code and data

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/xvr2e7/shibbo): MIT-licensed code; the registry is YAML in data/tells.yaml and data/tells.d/
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/shibbo)
